messages:
Maya C: heads-up — onboarding thread for cust 'echidna' LoRA merge. ran the first fast-eval pack and seeing weird numeric shift on invoice examples.
Samir: ok — which pack did you run? link? :eyes: 
Maya C: ran `./scripts/run-fast-eval --customer echidna --pack small-invoice --model base-7b+lora-merged` — logs at s3://redwood-evals/echidna/1708080808.log 
Samir: I pulled the log, looks like tokenization offset for amounts. sample: "Invoice total: $1,234" -> model outputs "Invoice total: 1234 dollars" which messes downstream matchers.
Rachit: that smells like tokenizer vs LoRA vocab alignment. Did the LoRA use an updated tokenizer or special tokens?
Maya C: customer LoRA uses custom special token <AMT> mapped in their finetune; we merged but didn't include tokenizer merge step. oops.
Julie: quick test — can you try shadow-patch with the customer's tokenizer added at merge time? I have a patch that updates tokenizer JSON and merges merges_vocabs.
Maya C: trying now. running small run with `--tokenizer-override echidna-tokenizer.json`
CI Bot: started smoke run for 1708080818 — job: eval-fast-eval-1708080818 on runner-14
Samir: also check int4 quantization path — we saw slightly different behavior under 4-bit; might amplify tokenization mismatch. what quant did you test?
Maya C: ran float16 first, then int4 quick-scan. int4 showed higher divergence on amount formatting (ROUGE-L drop ~0.12).
Rachit: that aligns — quant noise can push generation into alternate phrasing. Two mitigations: 1) ensure tokenizer merge is present; 2) run targeted calibration with a few batches to adjust KV scaling (we have a tiny script kv-calibrate.py).
Maya C: patched tokenizer, re-ran float16 pack. preliminary: amount format fixed for 94% of invoice cases. pushing int4 next.
CI Bot: eval-fast-eval-1708080818 completed: float16 pack -> 94% pass on invoice-amount; int4 pack queued.
Samir: if int4 still fails, try applying LoRA merge with weight-rescale option `--rescale 0.9` — sometimes helps with phrasing regressions. Not ideal but useful for quick unblock.
Maya C: int4 results in — still ~85% pass, but some hallucinated currencies (USD->EUR) in locale edge cases.
Rachit: currency swap could be locale token mapping. Can you share a failing example?
Maya C: example: input: "Total amount due: $47.50" -> output: "Montant total dû: 47.50 €" (random locale translation)
Julie: weird. Could be mixing in multilingual tokens from LoRA training set. Suggest augmenting eval pack with language-detection filter and penalize non-en outputs in scoring.
Samir: also check decoding params — temperature, top_p. Did fast-eval use greedy?
Maya C: default was top_p=0.95 temp=0.6 for generation. switching to greedy reduces hallucinations but hurts some long-form phrasing.
Rachit: for customer onboarding, prefer deterministic passes for numeric extraction tasks: greedy or beam width 2 plus a postprocess extractor. Keep probabilistic runs for human-eval.
Maya C: noted. Next steps: 1) upstream merge tokenizer into model artifacts (done) 2) rerun int4 with greedy + kv-calibrate 3) if still bad, try weight-rescale + small adapter patch 4) update eval pack to include locale checks and extraction-based scoring.
Julie: can you add those steps to the customer handoff doc? I'll prepare a quick PR for the eval pack changes.
Maya C: will add run outputs and failing cases to the thread. attaching snippet of failing outputs in S3.
CI Bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/echidna/1708080832/int4-run-results.json
Samir: thanks — ping me once int4 rerun is done and I'll take a look at the quant diagnostics. :thumbsup:
